function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.reasoning: The user wants to remove the timer.exe that was set earlier using the taskkill command. They likely want to kill the process and maybe delete the file. We need to use the tool to execute system commands. The user says "remove the timer.exe that i have been set earlier using the taskkill command". So we should run taskkill /IM timer.exe /F to force kill it. Then maybe delete the file: del timer.exe. But the user didn't specify deletion, just removal. Let's interpret as kill the process. We'll use the tool to run taskkill. We'll also confirm if it's running. We'll do taskkill /IM timer.exe /F. We'll then check if it's still running. We'll use tasklist. We'll combine commands: taskkill /IM timer.exe /F && tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq timer.exe". We'll pass unit? Not needed. We'll call the tool.
